definition: A technique where lower-precision rounding errors are simulated in forward and backward passes during model training to minimize post-quantization accuracy loss.
details: Unlike post-training quantization (PTQ) which quantizes frozen weights, QAT incorporates low-bit representation errors directly into the training loss function, enabling the network to learn weights inherently robust to reduced precision representations.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Quantization-Aware Training.

citation.title: Quantizing Deep Convolutional Networks for Efficient Inference: A Whitepaper
